baseball: compact sports field with a clear baseball diamond layout and surrounding open play area, distinguishing baseball from stadium by lacking a large enclosed spectator structure, from golf course by lacking expansive landscaped fairways, and from field by having a more regular sports-specific geometric pattern.
beach: bright shoreline region with clear sand-water boundary and open coastal texture, distinguishing beach from island by lacking a fully isolated landmass, from desert by direct water contact, and from sea ice by warmer sand-like coastal appearance rather than frozen bright surface.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land, distinguishing bridge from harbor by lacking dense dock-side maritime infrastructure, from river by being a discrete crossing rather than a continuous channel, and from overpass by more direct crossing over water or terrain rather than elevated road-junction structure.
dense_residential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal spacing, distinguishing dense residential area from medium residential area by much closer building intervals, from sparse residential area by far smaller spacing, and from commercial area by smaller repeated residential roofs rather than larger business blocks.
desert: broad barren region with dry homogeneous texture and very little vegetation, distinguishing desert from chaparral by weaker shrub texture, from field by lacking cultivated or organized surface patterns, and from beach by lacking a clear shoreline water boundary.
field: broad open land surface with relatively uniform texture, distinguishing field from meadow by more organized land appearance, from baseball by lacking sports-field geometry, and from desert by showing less barren arid texture.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with dark green natural texture, distinguishing forest from meadow by stronger canopy continuity, from chaparral by denser vegetation cover, and from mountain by weaker terrain relief and fewer exposed rocky slopes.
harbor: waterfront maritime area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent port infrastructure, distinguishing harbor from bridge by lacking a simple crossing structure, from river by stronger dock-water logistics organization, and from storage tank by clearer shoreline maritime context.
intersection: road junction where multiple transportation lines meet, distinguishing intersection from roundabout by lacking a central circular traffic island, from overpass by weaker elevation structure, and from parking by lacking organized parked-vehicle row layout.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture and weak structural boundaries, distinguishing meadow from forest by lacking dense canopy, from field by weaker man-made organization, and from sparse residential area by lacking repeated roof structures.
overpass: elevated crossing transport structure with visible grade separation, distinguishing overpass from bridge by stronger multi-road elevated traffic pattern, from intersection by clearer elevation and crossing structure, and from railway by lacking parallel rail-line texture.
parking: large open paved area with organized parking rows and vehicle-oriented layout, distinguishing parking from commercial area by weaker building-block dominance, from harbor by lacking strong dock-water context, and from intersection by stronger row-like parking organization instead of crossing-road geometry.
railway: elongated rail corridor with parallel tracks and linear transport structure, distinguishing railway from overpass by stronger track-line continuity, from river by rail-line texture rather than a water channel, and from parking by lacking vehicle-row organization.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks, distinguishing river from bridge by being a water body rather than a crossing, from harbor by weaker dock-side infrastructure, and from meadow by stronger water-channel continuity.
sparse_residential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density, distinguishing sparse residential area from dense residential area by much larger spacing, from meadow by repeated roof structures instead of open vegetation texture, and from field by clearer residential layout.
stadium: large sports complex with prominent field and stronger enclosure or spectator-related structure, distinguishing stadium from baseball by larger scale and stronger venue framing, from overpass by lacking transport-road geometry, and from storage tank by lacking circular industrial containers.
storage_tank: clusters of large circular industrial tanks with highly regular round geometry, distinguishing storage tank from harbor by weaker shoreline maritime context, from stadium by compact circular industrial units instead of a sports venue, and from circular farmland by lacking surrounding agricultural texture.
